current_state: Checked the actual statute directly (5 ILCS 140/2(a)), not just the internal memo's own conclusion: "'Public body' means all legislative, executive, administrative, or advisory bodies of the State... and all other municipal corporations, boards, bureaus, committees, or commissions of this State, any subsidiary bodies of any of the foregoing including but not limited to committees and subcommittees thereof..." That literal text is broader, and more genuinely ambiguous, than the internal memo's confident conclusion suggests -- CPD itself is a "municipal corporation," and a PAC does function as an "advisory body" to it, so the statute's own words don't rule out PAC coverage as cleanly as doc 5-17 asserts. That said, real countervailing facts do support the memo's bottom line: CPD's own Code of Conduct requires every PAC to independently register and maintain its own Not-For-Profit corporate status (Section G, already confirmed), and separately bars a PAC from binding CPD to anything (Section VI.C, item #291) -- both consistent with a PAC being treated as its own separate private entity that happens to advise CPD, not a subsidiary body CPD created and controls the way it would an internal committee. This is a real, close legal question, not a settled one -- doc 5-17's conclusion is plausible and probably right, but it deserves actual counsel review against the statute directly before being treated as final, not just an internal memo's own say-so.

Administratively, "Bongo Beach" does not yet exist as its own distinct entity anywhere in CPD's systems -- confirmed directly, not assumed: CPD's own official GIS FeatureServer (queried live for items #31/#32) shows Jackson (Andrew) Park as one single 551.52-acre polygon, park_no 19, with no carve-out, sub-polygon, or annotation for the beach at all. The same live query (items #52/#53) found no separate facility ID or metadata record either. Our own two boundary drafts -- G0-02 (PAC advisory scope) and NP-02 (park/property jurisdiction) -- are deliberately kept as two distinct, cross-linked records rather than assumed identical (item #33), but neither has actual surveyed coordinate geometry yet (item #30, geojson field confirmed null), and neither has been reviewed or confirmed by CPD.

Two pieces remain genuinely unresolved, not just undecided: the water/lake boundary (item #36 -- how the shoreline or submerged-land line is treated, tied to Illinois' Public Trust Doctrine, not yet researched) and the underlying Cook County parcel/PIN-level property record (item #34 -- CPD's park-level GIS polygon is confirmed, but a parcel-level lookup did not succeed). Adjacent-property identification (item #44) is still open fieldwork.

In short: "Where is Bongo Beach" has a confident, well-sourced physical answer and a completely open administrative one -- and closing that gap runs through the same single dependency everything else in this project runs through: CPD's still-pending Gate 0 determination (item #1).

The Beach House is the one clear exception: confirmed directly against the City of Chicago's own Landmark Designation Report, it was designated a Chicago Landmark on December 8, 2004, officially as the "63rd Street Bathing Pavilion" -- built 1919 by South Park Commission architects (Classical Revival/Prairie-influenced, 460x145 ft, poured "popcorn concrete"/marblecrete construction). CPD's own facility page confirms it operates and rents out the building directly (item #163), but the landmark designation is a real, binding constraint this project hadn't surfaced before this synthesis pass: any exterior alteration requires review by the Commission on Chicago Landmarks under the Chicago Landmarks Ordinance -- this applies regardless of whatever BBPAC's own eventual authority over the site looks like.

investigation: The independent advisory council structure -- bylaws, board, officers, committees, membership, elections, and the explicit distinction between Park District authority, Advisory Council authority, and community participation.
current_state:
Today: nobody yet, formally -- but a complete, internally consistent governance structure has been fully drafted and is ready to activate the moment CPD's recognition question resolves.

The council currently operates informally as a Founding Committee, not yet incorporated as a legal entity (item #2), and not yet CPD-recognized (item #1, "Gate 0," still pending -- no response received to the draft request letter, and whether it was even sent is unconfirmed). Because of that, several things that would normally exist for a functioning PAC simply don't yet: no officers have been elected (items #8/#12), no meetings have been held (item #17), and the advisory-authority boundary between the council and CPD hasn't been tested by any real conflict (item #21) because there's no real council yet to test it.

What does exist is a complete, ready-to-activate governance design: a full 30-article bylaws draft (doc 2-02), modeled on CPD's own PAC Bylaw Template plus the published bylaws of three comparable PACs (Jackson Park, Horner Park, Welles Park). It defines membership (open to all, Chicago residency required only for officer eligibility and full voting rights, per CPD's own rule -- item #7), an officer structure (President/VP/Treasurer/Secretary minimum, matching CPD's baseline -- item #12), an election procedure (item #8), an open-meetings commitment (item #17), and an explicit self-limiting statement of its own authority: "separate and independent, advisory only, cannot direct CPD employees, bind CPD, speak for CPD, or exercise CPD authority" (item #21, Bylaws Article 3).

One real structural tension runs through all of this, not yet resolved: CPD's own published Guidelines state the Park District recognizes only one registered PAC per park and bars joint/combined PACs unless CPD specifically approves one (items #1/#5/#6). The entire bylaws draft is written on the assumption that Gate 0 resolves in favor of an independently recognized council for this beach -- if CPD instead directs a JPAC-sub-committee model or something else entirely, the draft would need real revision before any adoption vote, not just a rename.

It doesn't yet, on either of the two tracks this question actually splits into -- and those two tracks are genuinely independent of each other, not the same question asked twice.

Track one is governance recognition: whether CPD grants a separately recognized PAC, a JPAC sub-council, or some other model (item #1, "Gate 0") -- still pending, no response received, and whether the request letter was even sent is unconfirmed. Legal incorporation (item #2) is intentionally on hold behind this.

Track two is administrative/systems recognition, and it's confirmed to be a completely separate question from track one -- not something that automatically follows once Gate 0 resolves. No independent facility ID exists for the beach in any CPD system checked (items #52/#75/#115), and no "child record" of any kind exists under Jackson Park's park_no 19 (item #76) -- but this synthesis surfaces something important: that's confirmed to be the unexamined DEFAULT of no one having created a separate record, not a deliberate CPD decision against one. The naming split already found elsewhere in this project runs through here too: CPD's own GIS/park registry uses only "Jackson (Andrew)" (items #113/#114), while CPD's own ActiveNet program-registration system and public activity listings already use "63rd Street Beach" as a real, functioning name -- meaning CPD's own systems already disagree with each other about this, independent of anything BBPAC does.

One genuinely new finding from this synthesis pass: item #4's full compliance crosswalk of the 30-article bylaws draft against CPD's own Guidelines found real, specific drafting bugs that should be fixed before any submission to CPD, not after -- (1) Article 14 sets quorum using an Illinois statutory default (10 members or 10%) instead of CPD's own required "majority of members" standard, suggesting it was drafted from the wrong source; (2) Article 7 omits the specific 30-day post-election deadline for the officer background check that the Code of Conduct actually requires; and (3) a still-unresolved 3-vs-4 member minimum discrepancy in Article 5, plus (4) a naming inconsistency in Article 20 between CPD's "PAC Governance Committee" and JPAC's "Complaint Review Committee" that needs direct confirmation from CPD's Department of Community Engagement (LCA). Submitting a bylaws draft with real compliance gaps could itself complicate or slow down CPD's Gate 0 response -- fixing these first is a genuine, actionable next step, not just a formatting nicety.
proposed_state: CPD's own internal systems -- park registry, facility ID, GIS metadata, budget/cost-center identity -- are updated to reflect Bongo Beach's recognized status, backed by the written determination (docs G0-04 / 1-32) rather than informal or public-facing perception alone.

item_label: How does the rest of Chicago know the change occurred?
investigation: GIS, maps, websites, signage, 311, emergency systems, public datasets, communications, and community outreach -- every public-facing and inter-agency system that currently says "Jackson Park" where it should eventually say "Bongo Beach Park," tracked one by one in Section XVII (Digital Identity), Section IV (City of Chicago Systems), Section XVI (Signage), and Section XXIV (Public Communication).
current_state:
Unevenly, and mostly not yet -- but "not yet" understates how mixed the current picture already is, independent of anything BBPAC does.

Some systems already treat the beach as its own distinct place: the City's Beach Water Quality Automated Sensors dataset names "63rd Street Beach" specifically (item #91), CPD's own ActiveNet program-registration system does the same (item #113, Section 746 synthesis), and independent map/review platforms (Apple Maps, TripAdvisor -- item #459) already list it as a distinct location, not merged into Jackson Park. Other systems don't: the City's park-boundaries open-data mirror shows no separate entry (item #91), and whether Chicago's 311 system or emergency dispatch conventions distinguish the beach from the rest of Jackson Park was genuinely not tested in this project (items #93/#96) -- made more urgent, not less, by a previously-confirmed geocoding gap (item #82) referenced there.

For anything BBPAC would actively publish or announce, the picture is consistently the same as elsewhere in this project: entirely within our own control technically (our own domain, our own boundary map, our own press materials -- items #456/#600/#595), but contingent on CPD's still-pending Gate 0 determination (item #1) for both timing and content -- and, separately, there is no CPD-published process for coordinating an announcement with JPAC or with CPD itself (item #596), so any real-world rollout would need direct, ad hoc coordination rather than following an established playbook. A boundary map published today would necessarily be illustrative, not survey-grade, since no actual surveyed coordinate geometry exists yet (item #600, consistent with item #745's own finding).

CPD's own top-level website and its facility pages for Jackson Park and 63rd Street Beach (items #452/#453/#454) are outside BBPAC's ability to edit directly -- any change there depends entirely on CPD acting on its own initiative once (and if) Gate 0 resolves.
proposed_state: Every public-facing and inter-agency system currently showing "Jackson Park" where it should show "Bongo Beach Park" -- GIS, maps, city websites, 311, emergency dispatch, signage, public datasets -- is updated and confirmed, tracked item-by-item across Sections IV, XVI, XVII, and XXIV, with a completion checklist confirming none were missed.
